questions.question: What was India’s overall score in the Corruption Perceptions Index (CPI) for the year 2024 released in February 2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**38**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **India's overall score in the Corruption Perceptions Index (CPI) for 2024** was **38**, as released in February 2025.
 
• The **Corruption Perceptions Index (CPI)** is an annual report published by **Transparency International** which ranks countries based on perceived levels of public sector corruption.
 
• The score of **38** indicates that India has a moderate corruption level, as the CPI scoring system ranges from **0 (highly corrupt)** to **100 (very clean)**.
 
• India's ranking in the CPI is influenced by factors such as **governance, transparency, and institutional integrity**.
 
• This score is consistent with India's ongoing efforts to combat corruption through measures like **Digital India initiatives, e-governance, and improved judicial mechanisms**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Corruption Perceptions Index (CPI):**

 
 
• The CPI is a globally recognized index published by **Transparency International**, a non-governmental organization headquartered in Berlin, Germany.
 
• It ranks countries based on perceptions of corruption in the **public sector**, using data from multiple surveys and expert assessments.
 
• A score of **0** represents a highly corrupt nation, while a score of **100** indicates a corruption-free nation.
 
• The index covers **180 countries** and territories worldwide.
 
 
 
• **India’s Performance in Recent Years:**
 
 
• India's CPI score has fluctuated between **36 and 40** in the last decade, reflecting challenges in governance and anti-corruption measures.
 
• In the CPI for 2023 (released in 2024), India's score was **36**, indicating a slight improvement in the 2024 score of **38**.
 
 
 
• **Global Trends in CPI:**
 
 
• Countries like **Denmark, Finland, and New Zealand** consistently rank at the top of the CPI with scores above **85**, reflecting low levels of corruption.
 
• Countries with the lowest scores include **Somalia, Syria, and South Sudan**, with scores below **15**, indicating severe corruption challenges.
 
 
 
• **Government Initiatives to Curb Corruption in India:**
 
 
• Implementation of the **Right to Information (RTI) Act** to enhance transparency and accountability in governance.
 
• Introduction of **e-Governance** initiatives like **Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT)** to reduce leakages in welfare schemes.
 
• Efforts to strengthen anti-corruption agencies like the **Central Vigilance Commission (CVC)** and the **Lokpal and Lokayuktas**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Methodology of CPI:**

 
 
• The CPI aggregates data from **13 different sources**, including surveys conducted by organizations like the **World Bank** and the **World Economic Forum**.
 
• These sources assess corruption in areas like **bribery, misuse of public funds, and nepotism**.
 
 
 
• **Examples of Anti-Corruption Success:**
 
 
• Countries like **Estonia** and **Georgia** have significantly improved their CPI scores by implementing **e-governance and judicial reforms**.
 
• India's initiatives like **GST implementation** and the **Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code (IBC)** have contributed to improving transparency.

questions.question: In February 2025, which Indian athlete broke the Asian short-track record in the 5000 m with a time of 12:59.77?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Gulveer Singh**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Indian long-distance runner **Gulveer Singh** created history in **February 2025** by breaking the **Asian short-track record** in the **5000 m** event.
 
• He clocked a remarkable time of **12:59.77** at the **BU John Thomas Terrier Classic** held in **Boston, USA**.
 
• With this performance, **Gulveer Singh** became the **first Indian athlete** to breach the **13-minute barrier** in the **5000 m** discipline (indoor/short track).
 
• The previous **Asian indoor record** was **13:09.43**, which was set by **El Hassan El-Abbassi** of **Bahrain** in **2012**.
 
• **Gulveer Singh** finished **second** in the race, finishing just behind **Yared Nuguse** of the **USA**, who won the event with a time of **12:56.46**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Gulveer Singh:**

 
 
• Hailing from **Sirsa, Uttar Pradesh**, he is a prominent figure in India's middle and long-distance running circuit.
 
• In **March 2024**, he set the **national record** in the **10,000 m** (outdoor) with a time of **27:41.81** at **The TEN** meet in **California**.
 
• He won the **bronze medal** in the **10,000 m** at the **2022 Asian Games** held in **Hangzhou, China**.
 
 
 
• **Avinash Sable:**
 
 
• He is another legendary Indian runner who holds the **outdoor national record** for the **5000 m** (**13:19.30**) and the **3000 m Steeplechase**.
 
• While **Gulveer Singh** broke the short-track record, **Avinash Sable** remains a dominant force in outdoor athletics and **Commonwealth Games** medalists.
 
 
 
• **Short-Track vs. Outdoor Records:**
 
 
• **Short-track** records (often referred to as **indoor** records) are maintained separately from **outdoor** records by **World Athletics**.
 
• Short-track races typically take place on a **200-meter oval**, whereas outdoor tracks are **400 meters** in length.
 
 
 
• **Other Options:**
 
 
• **Jacob Kiplimo** is a world-renowned long-distance runner from **Uganda** and a **World Half Marathon** record holder.
 
• **Yared Nuguse** is an **American** middle-distance runner who competed in the same race in **Boston** where **Gulveer Singh** set the record.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Training and Support:** **Gulveer Singh** trains under the guidance of coach **Scott Simmons** and is supported by the **JSW Sports** program and the **Athletics Federation of India (AFI)**.
 
• **Historical Context:** Entering the sub-13 minute club is considered a world-class milestone in long-distance running, placing **Gulveer Singh** among the elite athletes globally.
 
• **Year of Achievement:** This record was established on **February 1, 2025**, marking a significant start to the athletic season for **India**.
 
• **Venue:** The **Boston University (BU)** track is famous for being a "fast track," frequently producing record-breaking times due to its banking and surface quality.

questions.question: Who was the first Paralympic gold medalist to receive the Arjuna Award 2025 (Lifetime)?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Murlikant Petkar**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **Murlikant Petkar** was the first Indian Paralympic gold medalist and a recipient of the **Arjuna Award**.
 
• He won the gold medal in the **1972 Paralympics** held in Heidelberg, Germany, in the **50m freestyle swimming event**, setting a world record time of **37.33 seconds**.
 
• **Murlikant Petkar** was a former soldier in the Indian Army, where he served in the Corps of Electronics and Mechanical Engineers (EME) before sustaining injuries during the **1965 Indo-Pak war**.
 
• Despite his injuries, he pursued sports and represented India in events like swimming, javelin throw, and table tennis at the Paralympics.
 
• He was honored with the **Arjuna Award** for his contributions to sports, making him a trailblazer for Indian para-athletes.

questions.question: Which of the following national parks was designated as 58th tiger reserve of India in March 2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Madhav National Park**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In **March 2025**, the Government of India officially notified **Madhav National Park** as the **58th Tiger Reserve** of the country.
 
• It is located in the **Shivpuri district** of **Madhya Pradesh** and spans an area of approximately **354 square kilometers**.
 
• The designation was finalized following the recommendation and approval of the **National Tiger Conservation Authority (NTCA)** to ensure better protection and habitat management for the big cats.
 
• This declaration makes **Madhav National Park** the **eighth tiger reserve** in the state of **Madhya Pradesh**, further strengthening its reputation as India’s **"Tiger State"**.
 
• The primary objective of this designation is to facilitate the **re-establishment** of a breeding tiger population in the **Gwalior-Chambal region**, where tigers had historically roamed but had disappeared over the decades.
 
• ***Hence, the correct answer is Madhav National Park.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Panna National Park**:
 
 
• Located in **Panna and Chhatarpur districts** of **Madhya Pradesh**, it was declared a **Tiger Reserve** in **1994**.
 
• It is famous for its successful **Tiger Reintroduction Project** started in **2009** after the local tiger population had vanished.
 
• It is also home to the **Ken River**, which is part of the **Ken-Betwa river linking project**.
 
 
 
• **Pench National Park**:
 
 
• This park straddles the border of **Madhya Pradesh and Maharashtra**. It was designated a **Tiger Reserve** in **1992**.
 
• It served as the inspiration for **Rudyard Kipling’s** famous work, **"The Jungle Book"**, featuring the character **Mowgli**.
 
• The park is named after the **Pench River** that flows through it from north to south.
 
 
 
• **Kuno National Park**:
 
 
• Located in the **Sheopur district** of **Madhya Pradesh**, it gained global attention in **September 2022**.
 
• It is the site for the **Action Plan for Introduction of Cheetah in India**, where **African Cheetahs** from **Namibia** and **South Africa** were released.
 
• While it hosts a variety of predators, it has not yet been designated as a primary **Tiger Reserve**.
 
 
 
• **Madhav National Park History**:
 
 
• Established in **1958**, it was named after **Madho Rao Scindia**, the Maharaja of Gwalior.
 
• The park features the **Sakhya Sagar Lake**, a **Ramsar site**, and the **George Castle**, built at the highest point for **King George V**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Project Tiger**: Launched on **April 1, 1973**, from **Jim Corbett National Park**, it is a major conservation program to protect the **National Animal** of India.
 
• **National Tiger Conservation Authority (NTCA)**: A statutory body constituted under the **Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972**, responsible for the management of **Tiger Reserves**.
 
• **Conservation Status**: Tigers are listed as **Endangered** on the **IUCN Red List** and are included in **Schedule I** of the **Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972**.
 
• **Ecological Corridor**: The **Madhav Tiger Reserve** is vital as it acts as a bridge between the **Ranthambore Tiger Reserve** in **Rajasthan** and the **Kuno-Panna** landscape, facilitating the natural dispersal of **wildlife**.
 
• **Tiger Census**: India conducts a **National Tiger Estimation** every **four years**. According to recent reports, India holds more than **75%** of the world's **wild tiger population**.

b8

questions.question: How many new Khelo India Centres are planned by the Delhi Government in 2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**6 new Khelo India Centres**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Delhi Government** has announced the establishment of **6 new Khelo India Centres** in 2025 to promote sports and nurture young talent in the region.
 
• The initiative is part of the **Khelo India Scheme**, a flagship program by the Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports aimed at **revitalizing the sports culture** in India at the grassroots level.
 
• These centres will focus on identifying and training athletes in various disciplines, ensuring access to **quality infrastructure, coaching, and resources**.
 
• The centres are expected to cater to **young athletes**, providing them with opportunities to excel in national and international competitions.
 
• They will also align with the government's commitment to enhancing **sports infrastructure** and fostering youth engagement in sports activities across Delhi.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Khelo India Scheme:**

 
 
• **Launched in 2018**, the Khelo India Scheme aims to **develop sports infrastructure**, identify talent, and provide financial assistance to athletes.
 
• It covers various components such as **Talent Identification and Development**, **Sports for Women**, **Promotion of Rural and Indigenous Games**, and **Sports for Peace and Development**.
 
• The scheme also organizes the **Khelo India Youth Games** and **Khelo India University Games** to provide young athletes with a competitive platform.
 
 
 
• **Existing Sports Infrastructure in Delhi:**
 
 
• Delhi is home to several prominent sporting facilities, including the **Jawaharlal Nehru Stadium**, **Indira Gandhi Indoor Stadium**, and **Major Dhyan Chand National Stadium**.
 
• The establishment of new Khelo India Centres will further **enhance sports accessibility** and bridge the gap between aspiring athletes and professional training.
 
 
 
• **Impact of Khelo India Centres:**
 
 
• The centres will provide a **structured pathway** for young athletes to transition from grassroots to elite-level sports.
 
• They will also contribute to **community engagement** by encouraging local participation and fostering a culture of fitness and sportsmanship.
 
 
 
• **Delhi Government's Initiatives in Sports:**
 
 
• The Delhi Government has been actively promoting sports through initiatives like **Mission Excellence**, which provides financial support to athletes.
 
• The new Khelo India Centres will complement these efforts, ensuring a holistic approach to sports development in the region.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Khelo India Youth Games:**

 
 
• These games are organized annually and serve as a platform for young athletes to **showcase their talent**.
 
• The games include a wide range of sporting disciplines such as athletics, archery, basketball, boxing, football, gymnastics, judo, swimming, and more.
 
• The 2023 edition of the games was hosted in **Bhopal, Madhya Pradesh**.
 
 
 
• **Indigenous Sports Promotion:**
 
 
• As part of the Khelo India initiative, indigenous sports like **Kabaddi**, **Kalaripayattu**, **Kho-Kho**, and **Mallakhamb** are being promoted to preserve and popularize traditional games.
 
• This ensures the inclusivity and cultural representation of sports across India.

questions.question: What was the theme of National Doctor’s Day in 2025?

options.text: Family Doctors on the Front Line
Behind the Mask: Who Heals the Healers?

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Behind the Mask: Who Heals the Healers?**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **National Doctor’s Day** in India is celebrated every year on **July 1st** to honor the contributions of doctors in society and to pay homage to Dr. Bidhan Chandra Roy, a renowned physician and the second Chief Minister of West Bengal, whose birth and death anniversary coincide on this date.
 
• The theme of National Doctor’s Day in **2025** was **"Behind the Mask: Who Heals the Healers?"**__. This theme aimed to highlight the mental health challenges, emotional stress, and well-being of doctors, especially during the post-pandemic era.
 
• This theme brought attention to the need for providing support systems for **healthcare professionals**, who often experience **burnout, anxiety, and depression** due to their demanding roles.
 
• The global pandemic emphasized the critical role of doctors as front-line warriors, but it also revealed the emotional toll they endure while saving lives. The 2025 theme emphasized creating awareness and empathy for their struggles.
 
• Several healthcare organizations, governments, and institutions organized campaigns, seminars, and workshops on this day to address the importance of the **mental health of medical professionals**, ensuring their physical and emotional well-being.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Significance of National Doctor’s Day:**

 
 
• Celebrated annually to recognize the services and contributions of doctors to society.
 
• It is a day to honor the role of medical professionals in improving health outcomes and saving lives.
 
• It also serves as a reminder of the importance of healthcare accessibility and medical advancements.
 
 
 
• **Importance of the 2025 Theme:**
 
 
• The theme **"Behind the Mask: Who Heals the Healers?"**__ shed light on the increasing cases of stress and mental health concerns among medical professionals.
 
• It highlighted the need for addressing issues like **workplace stress, long working hours, and lack of emotional support** in the healthcare industry.
 
• Organizations encouraged doctors to seek professional help and emphasized the importance of peer support and counseling programs.
 
 
 
• **Other Recent Themes:**
 __
 
• 2023: **"Celebrating Resilience and Healing Hands"** – Focused on honoring the relentless efforts of doctors during challenging times.
 
• 2024: **"Healing Hands, Caring Hearts"** – Highlighted the compassionate role of doctors in patient care.
 
• 2025: **"Behind the Mask: Who Heals the Healers?"**__ – Emphasized the emotional and mental well-being of doctors.
 
 
 
• **Dr. Bidhan Chandra Roy:**
 __
 
• Born on **1 July 1882**, Dr. Roy was a celebrated physician, freedom fighter, and politician.
 
• He was instrumental in establishing medical institutions such as the **Indian Medical Association** and the **Medical Council of India.**
 
• He was posthumously awarded the **Bharat Ratna**, India’s highest civilian award, in **1961**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Mental Health of Doctors:**

 
 
• Studies indicate that a significant percentage of doctors experience **burnout** due to the high-pressure nature of their profession.
 
• The **World Health Organization (WHO)** emphasizes the importance of providing mental health support and resources for healthcare workers.
 
• In India, initiatives like **helplines and counseling services** have been introduced to address these issues.
 
 
 
• **Global Perspective:**
 
 
• Countries worldwide are taking steps to ensure the well-being of healthcare professionals, including **mandatory counseling sessions** and **reduced working hours**.
 
• The **COVID-19 pandemic** further accelerated discussions around the mental health of doctors and the need for systemic changes.

questions.question: Recognised for excellence in chess, which individual was honoured with the Major Dhyan Chand Khel Ratna Award in 2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Gukesh Dommaraju**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Gukesh Dommaraju**, popularly known as **Gukesh D**, was selected for the prestigious **Major Dhyan Chand Khel Ratna Award** in **2025** in recognition of his extraordinary achievements in the field of **Chess**.
 
• He created history by becoming the **youngest-ever challenger** for the **World Chess Championship** title after winning the **FIDE Candidates Tournament** held in **Toronto**, **Canada**, in **April 2024**.
 
• He played a instrumental role in India winning its first-ever **Gold Medal** in the **Open Category** at the **45th Chess Olympiad** held in **Budapest**, **Hungary**, in **September 2024**, where he also won an individual **Gold Medal** on the **first board**.
 
• The **Major Dhyan Chand Khel Ratna** is the **highest sporting honor** in India, awarded annually by the **Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports** for spectacular and most outstanding performance in the field of sports over a period of **four years**.
 
• Gukesh became a **Grandmaster** at the age of **12 years, 7 months, and 17 days**, making him the **third-youngest** person in history to achieve this title at that time.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Harmanpreet Singh**: 
 
 
• He is the **captain** of the **Indian Men's National Hockey Team**.
 
• Under his leadership, India won the **Bronze Medal** at the **Paris 2024 Olympics**.
 
• He was the **top scorer** of the **Paris Olympics** hockey tournament with **10 goals** and is widely regarded as one of the best **drag-flickers** in the world.
 
 
 
• **Praveen Kumar**: 
 
 
• He is a celebrated Indian **Para-athlete** specializing in the **High Jump**.
 
• He clinched the **Gold Medal** in the **Men's High Jump T64** event at the **Paris 2024 Paralympics** with an **Asian Record** jump of **2.08 meters**.
 
 
 
• **Anish Sarkar**: 
 
 
• He is a chess prodigy from **West Bengal** who made headlines in late **2024**.

• The first recipient of this award was the chess legend **Viswanathan Anand** in the year **1991-92**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The **Major Dhyan Chand Khel Ratna Award** carries a cash prize of **Rs. 25 lakh**, a **medallion**, and a **certificate**.
 
• **Gukesh D** reached a peak **FIDE live rating** of over **2790** in **2024**, solidifying his position among the **top 5** chess players globally.
 
• In **2023**, he surpassed **Viswanathan Anand** to become the **top-ranked Indian player** in the **FIDE rating list**, ending Anand's **37-year** reign as India's **number one**.
 
• The award ceremony usually takes place at the **Rashtrapati Bhavan**, where the **President of India** confers the honors upon the athletes.

questions.question: What change did the Banking Laws (Amendment) Act, notified in April 2025, make regarding bank nominee rules?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Allowed up to four nominees**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The **Banking Laws (Amendment) Act**, notified in **April 2025**, introduced a significant reform by allowing bank account holders to have up to **four nominees** for a single account.
 
• Previously, under the **Banking Regulation Act, 1949**, depositors were permitted to nominate only **one individual** to receive the proceeds of their deposits in the event of their death.
 
• This amendment provides depositors with the flexibility of **simultaneous and successive nominations**. This means they can specify the proportion of funds each nominee should receive or list them in a preferred order of succession.
 
• The primary objective of this change is to reduce the volume of **unclaimed deposits** in the Indian banking system, which has been a growing concern for the **Reserve Bank of India (RBI)**.
 
• By allowing multiple nominees, the government aims to ensure a smoother transition of assets to legal heirs or beneficiaries, thereby minimizing legal disputes and administrative hurdles for families of deceased depositors. Hence, the correct answer is Allowed up to four nominees.&l

questions.question: Who among the following was awarded Comeback of the Year at the 2025 Laureus Awards?

• **Rebeca Andrade**, a Brazilian artistic gymnast, was awarded the prestigious title of "Comeback of the Year" at the **2025 Laureus Awards**.

• **Rafael Nadal:** Another tennis icon who has battled injuries and continued to perform at the highest level in his career.
 
• **Tom Pidcock:** A British cyclist renowned for his achievements in mountain biking and road cycling after recovering from setbacks.

• The "Comeback of the Year" award highlights the **spirit of perseverance, determination, and excellence** in sports, inspiring millions worldwide.
 
• It serves as a reminder of how athletes can **overcome adversities** and achieve greatness through hard work and dedication.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Rebeca Andrade's Legacy:**

 
 
• She is an inspiration for athletes globally, especially for those coming from underrepresented regions in sports like Brazil.

• **Broader Impact of Laureus Awards:**
 
 
• The awards not only honor athletic achievements but also emphasize the role of sports in driving **social change, unity, and inspiration**.
 
• Their global outreach has helped highlight **stories of perseverance**, like that of Rebeca Andrade, to inspire others worldwide.

questions.question: Why was Acko General Insurance fined ₹1 crore by the Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India (IRDAI) in May 2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Payments to an unregistered intermediary**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India (IRDAI)** imposed a significant monetary penalty of **₹1 crore** on **Acko General Insurance** in **May 2025**.
 
• The penalty was levied following a regulatory investigation that uncovered **violations related to payments made to an unregistered intermediary**. According to **IRDAI** regulations, insurance companies are prohibited from transacting or paying commissions to entities that do not hold a valid license to act as an insurance intermediary.
 
• Investigations revealed that the company had entered into arrangements where payouts were channeled to entities that were not authorized under the **IRDAI (Registration of Insurance Marketing Firms) Regulations** or the **Insurance Act, 1938**.
 
• The regulatory body observed that such practices bypass the transparent commission structures mandated for the industry and can lead to higher costs for policyholders. ***Hence, the primary reason for the fine was payments to an unregistered intermediary.***
 
• This enforcement action is part of **IRDAI's** broader mandate to maintain market discipline and ensure that all stakeholders in the insurance distribution chain are properly regulated and accountable.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **IRDAI (Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India):**
 
 
• It is a statutory body formed under the **IRDA Act, 1999**. It serves as the apex regulatory authority for the insurance sector in **India**.
 
• Headquartered in **Hyderabad**, its primary objectives include protecting the interests of policyholders and regulating, promoting, and ensuring the orderly growth of the insurance industry.
 
 
 
• **Acko General Insurance:**
 
 
• Founded in **2016** by **Varun Dua**, it is a prominent **Insurtech** company in **India** that follows a direct-to-consumer model.
 
• The company specializes in **digital-first** insurance products, including motor, health, and electronics insurance, often leveraging data and technology to offer competitive premiums.
 
 
 
• **Insurance Intermediaries:**
 
 
• These include agents, brokers, corporate agents, and web aggregators who act as a bridge between the insurance company and the customer.
 
• Under **Section 42** of the **Insurance Act, 1938**, no person can act as an intermediary or receive remuneration for procuring insurance business unless they are registered with the **IRDAI**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **The Insurance Act, 1938:** This is the cornerstone legislation for insurance in **India**. **Section 40** of this Act specifically prohibits the payment of any commission or brokerage to any person for soliciting or procuring insurance business in **India**, unless that person is an authorized agent or intermediary.
 
• **Regulatory Compliance:** **IRDAI** conducts periodic inspections and **audits** of insurance firms. Non-compliance with the **Expenses of Management (EoM)** limits or unauthorized payouts often results in stiff penalties, as seen in the **2025** ruling against **Acko**.
 
• **Solvency Ratio:** While not the reason for this specific fine, **IRDAI** mandates a minimum **solvency ratio** of **1.5 (150%)** for all insurers to ensure they have sufficient capital to settle claims even during financial stress.
 
• **Impact of Penalties:** Fines of this nature serve as a deterrent to other players in the **Insurtech** and traditional insurance space, emphasizing that digital innovation must go hand-in-hand with strict **regulatory compliance**.

questions.question: Among India’s neighbours, which of the following countries have the better ranking than India in the Corruption Perceptions Index (CPI) for 2024, released by Transparency International in February 2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**China**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Corruption Perceptions Index (CPI)** is published annually by **Transparency International**, ranking countries based on perceived corruption levels in their public sector.
 
• In the **CPI for 2024**, released in **February 2025**, India ranked lower than **China**, signifying that China’s public sector is perceived as less corrupt than India’s.
 
• **China** has consistently scored higher than India in recent CPI rankings due to its stringent anti-corruption measures and reforms, including crackdowns on corrupt officials.
 
• The **CPI scores** are calculated using multiple data sources, including expert assessments and surveys conducted by independent institutions.
 
• Countries are ranked on a scale from **0 to 100**, where **0** indicates highly corrupt and **100** indicates very clean. China’s score is higher than India’s, indicating better performance in combating corruption.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Corruption Perceptions Index (CPI):**

 
 
• The CPI is a globally recognized metric that evaluates countries based on **corruption perception** in their public sector.
 
• It uses a combination of **expert surveys** and **business opinion polls** conducted by independent organizations.
 
• The CPI ranking provides insights into governance, transparency, and accountability in different nations.
 
• **Transparency International**, headquartered in Berlin, Germany, is the organization responsible for publishing the CPI.
 
 
 
• **China’s Anti-Corruption Efforts:**
 
 
• China has implemented several anti-corruption campaigns spearheaded by the Communist Party of China, targeting corrupt officials and practices.
 
• Notable initiatives include the **“Tigers and Flies” campaign**, focusing on corruption at both high-ranking and local levels.
 
• The establishment of agencies like the **National Supervisory Commission** strengthened oversight and enforcement mechanisms.
 
 
 
• **India’s Corruption Challenges:**
 
 
• India faces significant challenges in addressing corruption, including issues related to bureaucratic inefficiency, political interference, and lack of stringent enforcement of anti-corruption laws.
 
• Although initiatives like the **Lokpal Act** and digital governance reforms aim to combat corruption, implementation gaps remain.
 
• India’s CPI ranking is impacted by systemic issues such as **red tape**, lack of accountability, and opaque decision-making processes.
 
 
 
• **Other Neighboring Countries:**
 
 
• Countries like **Bangladesh, Pakistan, and Sri Lanka** have historically ranked lower than India in CPI due to higher perceived corruption levels.
 
• These countries often grapple with issues such as **weak governance**, lack of judicial independence, and political instability that exacerbate corruption.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Transparency International:**

 
 
• Founded in **1993**, Transparency International is a global non-governmental organization working to combat corruption.
 
• Its flagship **Corruption Perceptions Index** provides comprehensive data on corruption levels worldwide, influencing policy-making and governance reforms.
 
 
 
• **Global Trends in CPI:**
 
 
• Scandinavian countries like **Denmark**, **Finland**, and **Sweden** consistently rank among the least corrupt nations, scoring high in CPI rankings.
 
• Countries with strong institutions, transparent governance, and effective anti-corruption mechanisms generally perform better on the CPI scale.
 
 
 
• **India’s Initiatives Against Corruption:**
 
 
• India has introduced reforms like the **Right to Information (RTI) Act**, **Digital India campaign**, and **Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT)** to reduce corruption.
 
• While these measures have improved transparency, challenges like enforcement and accountability persist.

questions.question: The Constitution (Scheduled Castes) Order (Amendment) Bill, 2023 amends the Constitution (Scheduled Caste) Order 1950 with respect to which state?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Chhattisgarh**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Constitution (Scheduled Castes) Order (Amendment) Bill, 2023** was introduced and passed by the **Parliament of India** to amend the **Constitution (Scheduled Castes) Order, 1950**, specifically in its application to the state of **Chhattisgarh**.
 
• The primary objective of the bill is to include the **Mahara** and **Mahra** communities as synonyms for the **Mehra**, **Mahar**, and **Ganda** communities in the **Scheduled Castes** list of **Chhattisgarh**.
 
• The **Lok Sabha** passed the bill on **July 24, 2023**, and the **Rajya Sabha** gave its approval on **August 9, 2023**, during the **Monsoon Session**.
 
• This amendment ensures that members of these communities can avail of the benefits meant for **Scheduled Castes** in the state, including **reservation** in educational institutions and government jobs.
 
• The bill was moved by the **Union Minister for Social Justice and Empowerment**, **Shri Virendra Kumar**, to rectify discrepancies in the existing list. ***Hence, the correct answer is Chhattisgarh.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Article 341 of the Constitution:** 
 
 
• This article empowers the **President** to specify the castes, races, or tribes which shall be deemed to be **Scheduled Castes** in relation to a particular **State** or **Union Territory**.
 
• Once the initial list is notified by the **President**, any inclusion or exclusion from the list can only be done by an **Act of Parliament**.
 
 
 
• **The Constitution (Scheduled Castes) Order, 1950:** 
 
 
• This is the foundational **Presidential Order** that lists the various castes eligible for affirmative action in **India**.
 
• It has been amended several times over the decades (e.g., **1956**, **1976**, and **2002**) to reflect changing social dynamics and administrative corrections.
 
 
 
• **The Process of Inclusion:** 
 
 
• The process begins with a recommendation from the concerned **State Government**.
 
• It is then vetted by the **Registrar General of India (RGI)** and the **National Commission for Scheduled Castes (NCSC)**.
 
• After their concurrence, the proposal is placed before the **Union Cabinet** and finally introduced as a **Bill** in **Parliament**.
 
 
 
• **Chhattisgarh State Context:** 
 
 
• The state of **Chhattisgarh** was carved out of **Madhya Pradesh** on **November 1, 2000**.
 
• Since its formation, there have been several demands to include phonetic variations of existing **Scheduled Castes** and **Scheduled Tribes** to ensure legitimate beneficiaries are not excluded due to spelling errors or local nomenclature.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment:** This ministry is the nodal agency at the **Central Government** level for the welfare of **Scheduled Castes**.
 
• **Impact of the 2023 Bill:** By adding the **Mahara** and **Mahra** communities, the government addressed a long-standing demand for **social justice**, as these groups were historically denied benefits despite sharing the same socio-economic status as the **Mahar** or **Ganda** communities.
 
• **National Commission for Scheduled Castes (NCSC):** Established under **Article 338**, this constitutional body monitors safeguards provided for **Scheduled Castes** and participated in the consultative process for this **2023 Amendment**.
</ul

questions.question: Which individual, celebrated as India's first Paralympic gold medalist, was honoured with the Arjuna Lifetime Achievement Award in January 2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Murlikant Petkar**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Murlikant Petkar** was conferred with the prestigious **Arjuna Lifetime Achievement Award** in **January 2025** in recognition of his pioneering contributions to Indian sports.
 
• He holds the distinction of being **India's first Paralympic gold medalist**, a feat he achieved more than five decades ago.
 
• His historic **gold medal** was won at the **1972 Summer Paralympics** held in **Heidelberg, West Germany**.
 
• He competed in the **50m Freestyle swimming** event, where he set a **World Record** at the time with a finish of **37.33 seconds**.
 
• The award presented in **2025** serves to honor his legacy as the person who put India on the **Paralympic** map long before the nation became a regular contender for medals in the event.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Military Career and Injury:**
 
 
• Before becoming an athlete, Petkar was a soldier in the **Indian Army**, serving in the **Corps of Electronics and Mechanical Engineers (EME)**.
 
• He sustained severe injuries, including **nine bullet wounds**, during the **1965 Indo-Pak War** in the **Sialkot sector**, which led to him becoming paraplegic.
 
 
 
• **Multifaceted Athlete:**
 
 
• Petkar was a versatile sportsman; he initially represented India in **Table Tennis** at the **1968 Tel Aviv Paralympics**.
 
• Apart from swimming, he has also competed internationally in **Javelin Throw**, **Precision Javelin Throw**, and **Shot Put**.
 
 
 
• **National Honors:**
 
 
• He was awarded the **Padma Shri**, India's fourth-highest civilian award, in **2018** by the **Government of India**.
 
• His life story was the inspiration for the **2024 biographical film** titled **"Chandu Champion"**, directed by **Kabir Khan** and starring **Kartik Aaryan**.
 
 
 
• **Evolution of Awards:**
 
 
• The **Arjuna Award** is usually given for outstanding performance over the previous **four years**, but the **Lifetime Achievement** category recognizes legends whose impact spans decades.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Devendra Jhajharia:** He is another legendary para-athlete who won **two gold medals** in **Javelin Throw** (**2004 Athens** and **2016 Rio**) and served as a major inspiration for the current generation.
 
• **Mariyappan Thangavelu:** He won the **gold medal** in the **Men's High Jump T42** category at the **2016 Rio Paralympics**.
 
• **Deepa Malik:** She was the **first Indian woman** to win a **Paralympic medal**, securing a **silver** in **Shot Put** at the **2016 Rio Games**.
 
• **Significance of 1972:** Petkar's gold in **1972** was India's only individual **Olympic** or **Paralympic** gold until **Abhinav Bindra** won gold in **2008** and **Devendra Jhajharia** won in **2004**.
</ul

questions.question: As per the Sustainable Development Goals — National Indicator Framework Progress Report, 2025, published in June 2025, what percentage of the rural population used improved sources of drinking water during the year 2024–2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**99.62%**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Sustainable Development Goals — National Indicator Framework (NIF) Progress Report, 2025**, was released in **June 2025** by the **Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI)**.
 
• According to the report, during the assessment year **2024–2025**, the percentage of the **rural population** using improved sources of drinking water reached **99.62%**. ***Hence, the correct option is 99.62%.***
 
• This indicator is a vital metric under **SDG Goal 6**, which specifically targets **Clean Water and Sanitation** for all citizens.
 
• The data indicates a significant upward trajectory in rural infrastructure development, ensuring that nearly the entire rural landscape has access to safe and improved water sources.
 
• The report serves as a monitoring tool for the **United Nations' 2030 Agenda**, tracking India's specific progress through the **National Indicator Framework (NIF)**, which currently consists of over **300 indicators**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **SDG 6 (Clean Water and Sanitation):** 
 
 
• This goal aims to ensure the **availability and sustainable management of water** and sanitation for all by the year **2030**.
 
• India's commitment to this goal is reflected in large-scale schemes designed to eliminate the disparity between **urban** and **rural** access.
 
 
 
• **Jal Jeevan Mission (JJM):** 
 
 
• Launched on **15th August 2019**, this mission is a primary driver for the high percentage recorded in the 2025 report.
 
• The mission aims to provide **Functional Household Tap Connections (FHTC)** to every rural household, often referred to as **"Har Ghar Jal,"** by **2024-25**.
 
• It emphasizes **community-based management** and greywater treatment to ensure long-term sustainability.
 
 
 
• **Improved Sources of Drinking Water:** 
 
 
• This category includes **piped water** into dwellings, **public taps** or standpipes, **tube wells** or boreholes, protected dug wells, and **rainwater harvesting** systems.
 
• The use of improved sources is critical in reducing **water-borne diseases** such as cholera, dysentery, and typhoid in **rural India**.

• It coordinates with various **Central Ministries** and **State Governments** to collect authenticated data for the **SDG Progress Reports**.
 
 
 
• **National Indicator Framework (NIF):** 
 
 
• The **NIF** is the backbone of **SDG monitoring** in India, localized to suit the Indian context while remaining aligned with **Global Indicators**.
 
• The **2025 Progress Report** highlights that India has made "substantial progress" in **Goal 6**, with the rural drinking water target being one of the most successful outcomes.
 
• Data for this specific indicator is often sourced from the **Department of Drinking Water and Sanitation** under the **Ministry of Jal Shakti**.

• Her personal best of **6.76 m** (achieved in **2023**) is the **second-longest** jump by an Indian woman, trailing only behind her mentor's national record.
 
 
 
• **Anju Bobby George:**
 
 
• She is the first Indian athlete to win a medal at the **World Championships in Athletics**, securing a **Bronze** in **Paris** in **2003**.
 
• Her national record of **6.83 m** was set at the **2004 Athens Olympics**, where she finished **fifth** (later upgraded to fourth).
 
• She was awarded the **Padma Shri** in **2004** and the **Major Dhyan Chand Khel Ratna** in **2003** for her contributions to sports.

• **Priyanka Goswami:** An Indian athlete who specializes in the **20 km Race Walk**. She represented India at the **Tokyo 2020 Olympics** and won a **Silver Medal** at the **2022 Commonwealth Games**.
 
• **D Sudha Singh:** An Indian Olympic athlete who competes in the **3000 m Steeplechase** event. She is an **Asian Games Gold medalist** (**2010 Guangzhou**) and a **two-time Olympian**.

questions.question: Which former Olympic swimmer was elected as the first female and African President of the IOC in March 2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Kirsty Coventry**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Kirsty Coventry**, a legendary swimmer from **Zimbabwe**, was elected as the **President** of the **International Olympic Committee (IOC)** in **March 2025**.
 
• Her election is a landmark event in sporting history, as she became the **first woman** and the **first individual from the African continent** to lead the organization since its founding in **1894**.
 
• She succeeded **Thomas Bach**, who served as the **IOC President** for **12 years** from **2013 to 2025**.
 
• Coventry is one of the most decorated Olympians in history, having won a total of **7 Olympic medals** (including **2 Gold**, **4 Silver**, and **1 Bronze**) across the **2004 Athens** and **2008 Beijing** Olympic Games.
 
• Before ascending to the presidency, she held significant administrative roles, including serving as **Zimbabwe's Minister of Sport, Arts, and Recreation** and the **Chair of the IOC Athletes' Commission** from **2018 to 2021**.
 
• The election took place during the **143rd IOC Session** held in **Ancient Olympia, Greece**, where she secured the majority of votes against other prominent candidates.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **International Olympic Committee (IOC):**
 
 
• The **IOC** is a non-governmental sports organization based in **Lausanne, Switzerland**.
 
• It is the supreme authority of the **Olympic Movement** and is responsible for the supervision and administration of the **Summer** and **Winter Olympic Games**.
 
• The **Olympic Charter** governs the organization, outlining the rules and guidelines for the Games and the conduct of the committee members.
 
 
 
• **Kirsty Coventry’s Athletic Career:**
 
 
• Known as Africa's **"Golden Girl,"** she is the most successful African Olympian in the history of swimming.
 
• She competed in **five consecutive Olympic Games**, starting from **Sydney 2000** to **Rio 2016**.
 
• Her primary events were the **100m and 200m backstroke**, as well as individual medley events.
 
 
 
• **Other Options Overview:**
 
 
• **Penny Heyns:** A former **South African** swimmer who made history at the **1996 Atlanta Olympics** by winning gold in both the **100m and 200m breaststroke**.
 
• **Cathy Freeman:** An **Australian** former sprinter who specialized in the **400 meters** and famously won the gold medal at the **2000 Sydney Olympics**.
 
• **Inge de Bruijn:** A **Dutch** former competitive swimmer and **four-time Olympic champion** who held multiple world records in the early **2000s**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Historical Context:** Since **1894**, the **IOC** has had **eight presidents**, all of whom were men, and seven of whom were from **Europe** (with the exception of **Avery Brundage** from the **USA**).
 
• **Presidential Term:** Under the current **Olympic Charter**, the president is elected by secret ballot for an initial term of **eight years**, with the possibility of being re-elected for a second term of **four years**.
 
• **Diversity and Inclusion:** Coventry’s presidency is seen as a pivotal shift toward **gender equality** and **global representation** within the highest echelons of international sports governance.
 
• **Vision:** During her campaign, she emphasized **transparency**, the **protection of clean athletes**, and increasing the accessibility of sports in **developing nations**.
